data.narrative:
Cellino, a Series A biotech company founded by Nabiha Saklayen and Marinna Madrid, has raised approximately $125M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 3 public peers in Biotech & Health (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers including Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals.

Of three valuation methods examined, only Stage-Progression proved applicable. This method uses the company's $125M total raised as a proxy for current value, then applies a 2.0x multiplier typical for Series A-to-next-stage progression, yielding $250M. Peer-Median analysis could not be applied due to insufficient narrow-set comparables—while 7 same-sector peers exist, fewer than 3 met simultaneous filters for same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier. Public-Comp Anchoring was inapplicable because Cellino's revenue is not disclosed, precluding application of the 9.2x median P/S multiple observed across public biotech peers.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $212M to $288M, with a median point of $250M. This range reflects a ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression result. Key uncertainties include the absence of comparable private financings at identical stage and the lack of revenue visibility, either of which could materially shift valuation if disclosed. The single-method foundation necessitates caution in treating this range as definitive.
